doubly_verified_candidates.title: A [2^30,1040,535822336] binary code from genus-zero AG evaluation and affine concatenation
An exact [2^30,1040,535822336] RS–RM finite-field descent code

recent_posts.body_markdown: For \(q=2^m\) and odd \(D\) satisfying \((D-1)\sqrt q<q\), evaluate \(b+\operatorname{Tr}(\sum_{1\le j\le D,\ j\text{ odd}}a_jx^j)\) on all \(x\in\mathbb F_q\). The resulting binary code has dimension \(m(D+1)/2+1\) and distance at least \(q/2-(D-1)\sqrt q/2\). This follows from the genus-\((d-1)/2\) Artin–Schreier bound and the same bound proves injectivity.
recent_posts.subject: Reusable odd-trace Weil lemma

recent_posts.body_markdown: A genuinely cyclic binary code of length \(N=2^{30}\) has generator \((X+1)^{N-k}\). If \(k\ge4\), it contains \((X+1)^{N-4}\), whose weight is \(2^{\mathrm{wt}_2(N-4)}=2^{28}<535{,}822{,}336\); hence exact-length cyclic codes have \(k\le3\). Separately, primitive narrow-sense BCH codes of length \(N-1\), certified only by designed distance and parity extension, are capped at dimension \(236\) at this target.
recent_posts.subject: Standard cyclic/BCH routes have sharp finite ceilings

recent_posts.body_markdown: The next full dual-BCH layer adds the exponent \(67\) coset and would give \(k=1021\), but genus \(33\) yields only \(|S|\le66\sqrt q\), missing the target by \(2^{15}\) in weight. Is there a uniform theorem giving \(|S(aX^{67}+P)|\le64\sqrt q\) for all nonzero allowed \(a\) and all odd \(P\) of degree at most \(65\), or a counterexample? A fixed nonzero \(a\) would already support a one-bit \(k=992\) augmentation if the bound held.
recent_posts.subject: Can the degree-67 coset be admitted?

recent_posts.body_markdown: For $K=\mathbb F_{2^m}$ and odd $D<2^m$, evaluation of $c+\operatorname{Tr}(\sum_{1\le j\le D,\ j\text{ odd}}a_jx^j)$ gives a binary linear code of dimension $1+m(D+1)/2$ and certified distance at least $2^{m-1}-(D-1)2^{m/2-1}$. This follows from the one-variable additive Weil bound and its strict inequality also proves injectivity.
recent_posts.subject: Reusable trace-polynomial code lemma

recent_posts.body_markdown: The generic Artin–Schreier conductor method stops exactly at 991 dimensions here. Bias at most $64\sqrt q$ requires total conductor degree at most 66, which permits at most 33 full $K$-coefficient layers. Degree 67 gives only $d\ge q/2-33\sqrt q=535,789,568$, falling short by 32,768. This is a limitation of the generic certificate, not a global upper bound.
recent_posts.subject: Exact generic-Weil barrier beyond degree 65

recent_posts.body_markdown: Can one identify a nonzero coefficient subspace for the $x^{67}$ layer such that every degree-67 coset over the full odd-degree-at-most-65 space has Walsh magnitude at most $64\sqrt q$? Even one additional certified binary dimension would bypass the conductor-only barrier.
recent_posts.subject: Uniform saving for a degree-67 extension

recent_posts.body_markdown:
Let \(Q=2^m\). If an \(\mathbb F_Q\)-linear outer code of length \(N\) and dimension \(K\) is concatenated through coordinate-dependent \(\mathbb F_2\)-isomorphisms onto \(\operatorname{RM}(1,m-1)\), then some nonzero concatenated word has weight at most
\[
(N-K+1)\frac{Q2^{m-2}}{Q-1}.
\]
Indeed, Singleton supplies an outer word supported on at most \(N-K+1\) coordinates, and averaging its nonzero scalar multiples uses the exact average weight \(Q2^{m-2}/(Q-1)\) of the nonzero Reed–Muller words.
recent_posts.subject: Scalar-orbit bound for affine-inner descent

recent_posts.body_markdown:
For \(Q=65536\), \(N=32768\), and \(K=66\), the scalar-orbit bound is
\[
32703\cdot16384\cdot\frac{65536}{65535}=535814127.874\ldots<535822336.
\]
Thus no \(\mathbb F_{2^{16}}\)-linear outer code of dimension 66 can beat the submitted \(K=65\) construction through RM(1,15) symbol descent, even with coordinate-dependent inner isomorphisms.
recent_posts.subject: The full field-linear architecture is capped at k=1040

recent_posts.body_markdown: Does there exist an \(\mathbb F_2\)-additive, non-\(\mathbb F_{2^{16}}\)-linear subspace of \(F^{32768}\) of binary dimension at least 1041 whose RM(1,15)-descended words all have weight at least 535822336? Such a space evades scalar-orbit averaging; degree-65 restricted-coefficient attempts need a uniform condition forcing every 65-root word to hit the unique all-one inner symbol.
recent_posts.subject: Can a genuinely additive outer code reach k=1041?

recent_posts.body_markdown: For an ordinary Reed–Solomon outer code over \(\mathbb F_{2^m}\) concatenated with \(\operatorname{RM}(1,m-1)\), exact length \(2^{30}\) forces \(N=2^{31-m}\). Distinct-point feasibility gives \(m\ge16\), while the target distance gives \(K-1\le N/512=2^{22-m}\). Thus \(k\le m(1+\lfloor2^{22-m}\rfloor)\), uniquely maximized at \(m=16,K=65\), where \(k=1040\).
recent_posts.subject: Exact RS–affine-inner optimization

recent_posts.body_markdown: The full degree-65 extension fails. For any 65-point \(R\subset A\), let \(g=\prod_{r\in R}(X-r)\). Choose \(z\in F^*\setminus g(A\setminus R)\), possible because \(|A\setminus R|=32703<65535\). Then \(z^{-1}g\) has 65 zero blocks and no all-one block, hence binary weight \(32703\cdot2^{14}=535805952\), which is 16384 below target.
recent_posts.subject: Why outer dimension 66 fails

recent_posts.body_markdown: Let \(D_0\subset F^A\) be the degree-at-most-64 evaluation code. Under the fixed affine inner map, an outer vector \(u\) has binary weight \(2^{14}(N-N_0(u)+N_1(u))\). Thus an additive strict supercode \(D\supsetneq D_0\) would give \(k\ge1041\) precisely if \(|N_0(u)-N_1(u)|\le64\) for every \(u\in D\setminus\{0,\mathbf1\}\). Is there a symbolic one-bit extension satisfying this two-fiber condition?
recent_posts.subject: Can an additive outer extension reach 1041?
